title: CSGPath generation 'up' vector drifts when using path follow mode
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in Godot v4.6.2.stable ### System information Godot v4.6.2.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Ti SUPER (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - AMD Ryzen 7 3700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 15.92 GiB memory ### Issue description When using `path_rotation=Path` the rotation is ignored, but also tilt is ignored. When using `path_rotation=PathFollow` you can use tilt, but the shape brush rotates near the end of the curve (tilt=0): This behavior doesn't happen with `PathFollow3D` nodes. (If you set the rotation_mode=oriented) which allows the `PathFollow3D` node to point 'up' properly at the end of the same curve ### Steps to reproduce Create a CSGPolygon3D inside of a path3D node with these settings: ``` path_rotation = 2 path_rotation_accurate = true path_local = true path_continuous_u = true path_u_distance = 1.0 ``` Create a Curve3D for the Path3D and have it curve 90 degrees over 5 meters and descend 1 meter. The cap at the end of the CSGPolygon3D shape is tilted, even though the curve has no tilt.. (see MRP) ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [repro-csgpath-rotation.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26586100/repro-csgpath-rotation.zip)
